title: Decouple timeouts and implement regional bandwidth-aware priority scheduler for rerank
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Production reranker endpoints are experiencing two correlated failure modes during regional spikes: (1) coarse-grained end-to-end timeouts cause useful progress to be dropped when a single stage (embedding fetch, candidate scoring, or final rerank) is slow, and (2) naive fanout across regions amplifies tail latency and capacity pressure, producing cascading circuit-breaker trips. This ticket proposes decoupling per-stage timeouts, introducing a regional bandwidth-aware priority scheduler that shapes fanout, and adding a lightweight local fallback reranker to preserve quality under degraded conditions.

Goals: 
- Reduce P99 end-to-end latency and tail variance for rerank requests under cross-region load.
- Reduce incidents caused by global circuit-breaker cascades.
- Maintain downstream quality by using a graceful fallback that trades off a small amount of accuracy for continuity.

Design: 
1) Per-stage timeouts and soft-deadlines: split the rerank pipeline into explicit stages with independent soft timeouts: embedding fetch (E), candidate scoring (S), and final rerank/sort (R). Each stage exposes a "soft deadline" to upstream stages so partial results can be surfaced. Soft deadlines are conservative (e.g., 70% of end-to-end SLO) and fall back to the next-best available data when missed.

2) Regional bandwidth-aware priority scheduler: a new scheduler component will run in each region that: (a) tracks per-region capacity and recent success ratios; (b) applies token/bandwidth budgets per-customer and per-route; (c) converts incoming requests into a prioritized fanout plan (local-first, regional-prefetch, remote-probe) rather than blind broadcast. Requests marked high-priority (SLA customers or interactive flows) get aggressive local prefetch and hedging; low-priority batch flows are buffered or deferred.

3) Hybrid fallback reranker: a lightweight on-host approximate reranker (quantized MLP or tiny cross-encoder) seeded from cached embeddings will be used as a best-effort fallback when remote scoring is not returned before the soft deadline. The fallback preserves ordering for ~85-92% of pairs in our internal evals while reducing cost and latency.

4) Circuit-breaker policy tuning: replace the existing single global CB with a multi-dimensional CB keyed by (region, model-variant, customer-tier) using an exponential moving window for success ratio and dynamic cooldown that is aware of pending retries. CB decisions are surfaced to the scheduler for proactive routing adjustments.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Proto for per-stage soft deadlines in a canary branch; add instrumentation hooks for E/S/R timings (ENG-77502).
- Week 2: Implement the regional scheduler controller with a dry-run mode (no enforced routing) and dashboards (tokens/sec, queued, per-region success ratio).
- Week 3: Integrate lightweight fallback reranker and add opt-in via per-customer feature flag.
- Week 4: Canary rollout to sandbox accounts and targeted customers; collect quality/regression metrics; iterate on timeout thresholds.
- Week 5: Gradual rollout with runtime-1.23 canary -> stage -> global.

Metrics and dashboards: 
- SLOs: P50/P95/P99 latency for rerank end-to-end and per-stage.
- Quality: rerank NDCG@10 drop when fallback used; fraction of requests served by fallback.
- Reliability: circuit-breaker trips per region, success ratio windows, regional capacity utilization.
- Cost: extra local CPU/GPU used for fallback, cross-region egress reduction.

Testing: 
- Unit tests for deadline propagation and stale-result handling.
- Load tests simulating region-wide congestion and partial network partitions.
- Regression checks against canonical rerank eval sets to ensure fallback quality >= 85% of baseline.

Rollout and safety: 
- Feature flags per-customer and per-route for fallback and scheduler enforcement.
- Canary in a single region with synthetic traffic emulating heavy incomplete fanouts.
- Automatic rollback triggers: >10% regression in NDCG@10 or >3x increase in error rate.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Fallback ordering degrades user-facing features. Mitigation: conservative flagging, gradual rollout, add a post-fallback scoring illumination log to trace when fallback used.
- Risk: Scheduler misconfiguration may starve background workloads. Mitigation: quotas and per-tenant minimum throughput reservations.
- Risk: Added complexity in CB keying leads to false positives. Mitigation: tune with longer smoothing windows and shadow mode before enforcement.

Artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/rerank-scheduler-prd, Design notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/rerank-scheduler-design-v1, Eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-evals/pulls/519, Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/rerank-scheduler-canary

Next steps: finalize API for stage deadlines, finish scheduler dry-run and dashboards, and schedule architecture review with infra and security for cross-region behavior.
